rounds.text: Yuranus Infrastructure Ltd demonstrates exceptional medium-to-long-term compounding power, highlighted by compounded sales growth of 200% over 3 years, 106% over 5 years, and 61% over 10 years [E14, E15, E16]. This rapid top-line expansion is translating directly into exceptional bottom-line acceleration, with compounded profit growth reaching 185% over the trailing twelve months and 114% over 3 years [E20, E21], alongside a net profit surge exceeding 600% year-over-year [E65]. Operating profitability has undergone a massive structural improvement, with operating margins expanding by 43 percentage points over three years to reach 10% in March 2026, supported by an increasing quarterly trend over the last four consecutive quarters [E30, E33]. Efficiency metrics also shine as the company generates a superior return on capital employed of 13% and an ROE of 10.57%, both comfortably outperforming respective sector benchmarks of 3.14% and 5.78% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, institutional sponsorship is validating this fundamental turnaround, with foreign institutions building a 3.66% stake up from zero in September 2023 [E42], while management demonstrates prudent financial stewardship by actively reducing total borrowings down to ₹ 1.89 Cr [E39]. Conceded: [E1] and [E2] show that the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 82.6 and price-to-book of 8.76x, while [E44] and [E60] note negative free cash flow and rising debtor days.

Conceded: [E14], [E15], [E16], [E20], [E21], [E42], and [E65]. While the bull highlights rapid multi-year growth and recent foreign institutional accumulation, top-line momentum has severely collapsed with trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth plunging to -61% [E17]. The bull's reliance on backward-looking profit expansion ignores extreme valuation disconnects, including a lofty P/E of 82.6x against a sector benchmark of 33.03x and a Price-to-Book multiple of 8.76x [E1, E2, E6]. Furthermore, reported profit growth is entirely disconnected from cash generation; cash conversion sits at a miserable 0.06x for March 2026, with operating cash flow making up just 14% of operating profit and resulting in negative free cash flow of Rs -0.02 Cr [E34, E36, E37]. This alarming disconnect is compounded by deteriorating collection efficiency, as debtor days have ballooned from 37.7 to 83.1 days and working capital days have surged to 88.2 days [E60, E61]. Finally, the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a lagging relative-strength rating of 16, while a reverse DCF reveals the market is already pricing in an aggressive 25.1% earnings growth rate [E46, E49, E50].
